name: Another Life
description: Another Life makes hospitality furniture from repurposed teak. Danish design, made in Indonesia, shipped flat and built to be repaired.
purpose: We exist to make furniture that lasts a long time.
customers: Boutique hotels, resorts, restaurants and cafés, and the architects and interior designers who work with them

material.name: Repurposed teak
material.source: Often old joglo houses in Indonesia, also bridges, boats and other structures

finish.name: Shou Sugi Ban
finish.process: Flame-darkened teak, finished with natural oil to preserve the character of the wood.
finish.standard: Marks from the wood's first life stay visible, never at the cost of strength.
finish.note: Japanese yakisugi was made for softwood (cedar); Another Life applies it to hardwood teak. The aim is to help the wood handle strong sun; this has not been formally tested.

point_of_view.headline: Use it again, before you make it again.
point_of_view.summary: Long life beats recycling. Recycling ends a product's life and costs energy to make something new, so it is the last stop, not plan A. Order of preference: use, repair, take apart and store, rebuild, recycle.
point_of_view.analogy: A refillable glass bottle is better than one melted down into a new bottle.

lifecycle: Made by hand from wood that has already lived once.
Shipped flat and bolted together on site.
Used every day: a dining room, a terrace, a pool.
A part wears out: swap just that part.
The place renovates or closes: take it apart, store it flat.
Someone gives it a new place and a new purpose. Back to step 3.

mission_goals.status: Goals, not yet achieved. Another Life has just launched.
goals: Plant new trees for the wood we use
Give back to the communities and makers behind the furniture
Collaborate with planting projects, NGOs, hotels, architects, makers and community initiatives

hardware: Engineered stainless steel (SUS) bolts in threaded inserts, three-bolt clusters at each main joint, designed to outlast the furniture
construction: Knock-down: travels flat and is assembled on site
Comes apart without damage and goes back together as it was
If one part reaches its end, you replace the part, not the piece

philosophy.name: Conscious Sustainability
philosophy.core_line: A label is not a mission. Sustainability isn't a label you put on a product; it's a responsibility you build into it.
philosophy.position_on_certification: Certifications have their place, but no single label tells the whole story (lifespan, making, repairability, end of life). Another Life aims to show sustainability through what it makes rather than rely on a label alone.
philosophy.claims_policy: Never claim a piece is completely sustainable; never publish unverified carbon or transport figures.

traceability.name: Another Life Passport
traceability.description: A QR tracing system that tells the story of each piece: origin, making, journey, care and repair
intended_questions: Where did the material come from?
What happens at the end of its first life?

taglines: Made for this life. And another.
Make it once. Let it live.
Sustainability is for everyone. Conscious style is not.
Another material. Another owner. Another place. Another life.
Materials from another life. Designed for another life.
Made from what came before. Made for what comes next.
A label is not a mission.

products.name: The Chair
products.description: A knock-down dining chair in repurposed teak. It travels flat, goes together on site and is designed to be repaired for decades rather than replaced.

products.name: The Sun Lounger
products.description: A slatted sun lounger in repurposed teak with an adjustable backrest, made for pools and gardens. It travels flat and goes together on site.

products.name: The Bench
products.description: A long slatted bench in repurposed teak, 206 cm long, at the same seat height as The Chair.

products.name: The Lounge Chair
products.description: A low, deep chair in repurposed teak with a 32 cm seat height, for lounges, lobbies and terraces.

products.name: The Side Table
products.description: A low square table in repurposed teak, 75 by 75 cm, at the same height as the seats of the loungers and The Lounge Chair.

products.name: The Coffee Table
products.description: A low table in repurposed teak, 75 by 100 cm, made to sit between Lounge Chairs in lounges, lobbies and terraces.

products.name: The Table
products.description: A dining table in repurposed teak, 100 by 220 cm, made to sit with The Chair and The Bench.

glossary.SATU: The first Another Life collection: The Chair, The Sun Lounger, The Bench, The Lounge Chair, The Side Table, The Coffee Table and The Table.
glossary.Repurposed teak: Teak that has already been cut and used. Much of ours comes from old joglo houses.
glossary.Joglo: A traditional Indonesian house built in teak. Much of the timber we reuse comes from old joglo houses.
glossary.Shou Sugi Ban: A Japanese technique of charring wood with flame, known in Japan as yakisugi and made for cedar. We apply it to hardwood teak and finish it with natural oil.
glossary.Knock-down: Furniture that ships disassembled and bolts together on site. Ours is designed to be taken apart and reassembled more than once.
glossary.Conscious Sustainability: Our way of judging materials and methods. No single material or label is sustainable everywhere, so we look at origin, production, longevity, transport, repairability and documentation.
glossary.Another Life Passport: Our QR tracing system: a code on each piece that opens its own story, from its first life to its next.
